animation: none !important; }\n}\n</style>\n</head>\n<body>\n<a class=\"skip\" href=\"#main\">Skip to main content</a>\n\n<nav class=\"topnav\" data-scrollspy aria-label=\"Section navigation\">\n<a href=\"#hero\">Overview</a>\n<a href=\"#contributions\">Contributions</a>\n<a href=\"#method\">Method</a>\n<a href=\"#results\">Results</a>\n<a href=\"#figures\">Figures</a>\n<a href=\"#limitations\">Limitations</a>\n</nav>\n\n<nav class=\"sidenav\" data-scrollspy aria-label=\"Section navigation\">\n<a href=\"#hero\">Overview</a>\n<a href=\"#contributions\">Contributions</a>\n<a href=\"#method\">Method</a>\n<a href=\"#results\">Results</a>\n<a href=\"#figures\">Figures</a>\n<a href=\"#limitations\">Limitations</a>\n</nav>\n\n<main id=\"main\">\n<div class=\"wrap\">\n\n<!-- HERO -->\n<section class=\"hero\" id=\"hero\">\n<h1>Host vocabulary predicts whether new scientific concepts take root across disciplinary boundaries</h1>\n\n<p class=\"tldr\">When a new scientific concept first appears in a disciplinary subfield, does the vocabulary of its initial partner terms predict whether newcomer scientists will adopt it? Across 426 emerging concepts and 462,812 works from OpenAlex, the answer is yes: a one-standard-deviation increase in the share of entry partners belonging to the host field's vocabulary raises five-year newcomer uptake by 23% (incidence-rate ratio 1.23, 95% CI 1.12 to 1.36), replicated on an independent population of 191 MeSH biomedical concepts.</p>\n\n<div class=\"doc-links\">\n<a href=\"https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8892b7-occupancy-is-not-integration-for-new@fork/run_YczZzZ0_9kfq/paper.pdf\">Read the paper (PDF)</a>\n<a href=\"https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8892b7-occupancy-is-not-integration-for-new@fork/run_YczZzZ0_9kfq/report.pdf\">Read the full research report</a>\n<a href=\"https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8892b7-occupancy-is-not-integration-for-new@fork/run_YczZzZ0_9kfq/exec_summary.pdf\">Read the executive summary</a>\n<a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8892b7-occupancy-is-not-integration-for-new/tree/fork/run_YczZzZ0_9kfq\">Code repository</a>\n</div>\n<div class=\"round-links\">\nRound reports:\n<a href=\"https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8892b7-occupancy-is-not-integration-for-new@fork/run_YczZzZ0_9kfq/round-1/report.pdf\">Round 1</a>\n<a href=\"https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8892b7-occupancy-is-not-integration-for-new@fork/run_YczZzZ0_9kfq/round-2/report.pdf\">Round 2</a>\n<a href=\"https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8892b7-occupancy-is-not-integration-for-new@fork/run_YczZzZ0_9kfq/round-3/report.pdf\">Round 3</a>\n<a href=\"https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8892b7-occupancy-is-not-integration-for-new@fork/run_YczZzZ0_9kfq/round-4/report.pdf\">Round 4</a>\n<a href=\"https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8892b7-occupancy-is-not-integration-for-new@fork/run_YczZzZ0_9kfq/round-5/report.pdf\">Round 5</a>\n</div>\n</section>\n\n<!-- CONTRIBUTIONS -->\n<section id=\"contributions\">\n<h2>Contributions</h2>\n<div class=\"cards\">\n\n<div class=\"card\">\n<h3>Host-entry grafting predicts adoption</h3>\n<p>When a concept enters a new subfield, the share of its entry partners belonging to the host vocabulary predicts five-year newcomer uptake. Pre-registered and replicated on an independent MeSH biomedical population (co-primary IRR 1.23, 95% CI 1.12 to 1.36; verdict: REPLICATED). Development-set estimates are concordant: Screen IRR 1.30, Held-out IRR 1.19.</p>\n<div class=\"cl\">\n<a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8892b7-occupancy-is-not-integration-for-new/tree/fork/run_YczZzZ0_9kfq/round-3/experiment-7\">Code: Do borrowed ideas stick when grafted locally?</a>\n<a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8892b7-occupancy-is-not-integration-for-new/tree/fork/run_YczZzZ0_9kfq/round-4/evaluation-2\">Code: One-time held-out check of the idea-grafting result</a>\n<a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8892b7-occupancy-is-not-integration-for-new/tree/fork/run_YczZzZ0_9kfq/round-4/experiment-9\">Code: Idea grafting replicates in biomedical MeSH concepts</a>\n</div>\n</div>\n\n<div class=\"card\">\n<h3>Outcome-blind concept dataset</h3>\n<p>A semantically grounded, outcome-blind dataset of 426 emerging concepts with 462,812 OpenAlex works across physics, computer science and biomedicine, plus an independent check population of 191 MeSH biomedical concepts.</p>\n<div class=\"cl\">\n<a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8892b7-occupancy-is-not-integration-for-new/tree/fork/run_YczZzZ0_9kfq/round-1/dataset-1\">Code: New science concepts and their papers</a>\n<a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8892b7-occupancy-is-not-integration-for-new/tree/fork/run_YczZzZ0_9kfq/round-2/dataset-5\">Code: All concept papers downloaded, with field labels</a>\n<a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8892b7-occupancy-is-not-integration-for-new/tree/fork/run_YczZzZ0_9kfq/round-1/dataset-3\">Code: New MeSH medical terms as a held-out check set</a>\n</div>\n</div>\n\n<div class=\"card\">\n<h3>Host-specific effect through two margins</h3>\n<p>The host-vocabulary effect is host-specific rather than a proxy for generic concept accessibility, and it operates through both the extensive margin (whether uptake starts, +6.4 pp per SD) and the intensive margin (its magnitude, IRR 1.18). No detectable variation by origin field.</p>\n<div class=\"cl\">\n<a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8892b7-occupancy-is-not-integration-for-new/tree/fork/run_YczZzZ0_9kfq/round-5/evaluation-6\">Code: Does host vocabulary start uptake or grow it?</a>\n<a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8892b7-occupancy-is-not-integration-for-new/tree/fork/run_YczZzZ0_9kfq/round-5/evaluation-7\">Code: Host-specific or just common words?</a>\n</div>\n</div>\n\n<div class=\"card\">\n<h3>Structural precursors of emergence</h3>\n<p>Persistent-neighbour closure is lower before sustained uptake (S = &#x2212;1.07, Holm p = 0.015; development-set estimate). General closure fails on the Held-out fold. The effect is not Burt brokerage: emerging concepts sit in more constrained, not less constrained, ego networks.</p>\n<div class=\"cl\">\n<a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8892b7-occupancy-is-not-integration-for-new/tree/fork/run_YczZzZ0_9kfq/round-3/experiment-5\">Code: Is openness before take-off brokerage or churn?</a>\n<a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8892b7-occupancy-is-not-integration-for-new/tree/fork/run_YczZzZ0_9kfq/round-4/evaluation-3\">Code: One-time held-out check of closure and D3 link</a>\n</div>\n</div>\n\n<div class=\"card\">\n<h3>Diffusion typology and adopter enrichment</h3>\n<p>A stable two-type typology (localised vs. broad), an expansion-before-diffusion ordering (25 of 26 cases), and adopter-level enrichment for prior exposure to the concept's entry partners (OR 3.09; Screen fold, not independently confirmed).</p>\n<div class=\"cl\">\n<a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8892b7-occupancy-is-not-integration-for-new/tree/fork/run_YczZzZ0_9kfq/round-3/experiment-8\">Code: How new concepts spread: types, roles, timing</a>\n<a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8892b7-occupancy-is-not-integration-for-new/tree/fork/run_YczZzZ0_9kfq/round-4/evaluation-4\">Code: Checking concept spread types on unseen and medical data</a>\n<a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8892b7-occupancy-is-not-integration-for-new/tree/fork/run_YczZzZ0_9kfq/round-4/evaluation-5\">Code: Do adopters already know the partner words?</a>\n</div>\n</div>\n\n</div>\n</section>\n\n<!-- METHOD -->\n<section id=\"method\">\n<h2>Method</h2>\n\n<figure>\n<img class=\"method-fig\" src=\"figures/fig1_v0.jpg\"\n  alt=\"Study design diagram with four panels: data sources showing 426 arXiv concepts split into screen and held-out folds plus 191 MeSH concepts drawn from 462,812 OpenAlex works; co-word network of 25 yearly snapshots with approximately 27,000 nodes and 84,000 edges with Leiden communities; RQ1 matched event study comparing closure before sustained uptake; RQ2 host-entry grafting measuring host-vocabulary share to predict newcomer uptake\"\n  tabindex=\"0\" role=\"button\" aria-label=\"Enlarge Figure 1: Study design and analysis pipeline\"\n  data-lb-src=\"figures/fig1_v0.jpg\"\n  data-lb-title=\"Figure 1. Study design and analysis pipeline\">\n<figcaption style=\"font-size:14px;color:var(--text-sec);margin-top:8px;\">\n<strong style=\"font-size:15px;color:var(--text);display:block;margin-bottom:2px;\">Figure 1. Study design and analysis pipeline</strong>\n</figcaption>\n</figure>\n\n<h3>Data</h3>\n<p>The study tracks 426 emerging scientific concepts, assembled as an outcome-blind pool from arXiv noun phrases that first appeared in OpenAlex between 2005 and 2016 (<a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8892b7-occupancy-is-not-integration-for-new/tree/fork/run_YczZzZ0_9kfq/round-1/dataset-1\">code</a>). Of these, 366 are main emerging concepts (247 Screen fold, 119 Held-out fold) and 60 are stationary references. A logistic-regression classifier (F1 = 0.82, AUC = 0.89) and a variant merger (B-cubed F1 = 0.78) grounded every concept (<a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8892b7-occupancy-is-not-integration-for-new/tree/fork/run_YczZzZ0_9kfq/round-2/experiment-1\">code</a>). The pool is dominated by physics and computer-science concepts from arXiv.</p>\n\n<p>An independent biomedical arm of 191 concepts was drawn from new MeSH descriptors (<a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8892b7-occupancy-is-not-integration-for-new/tree/fork/run_YczZzZ0_9kfq/round-1/dataset-3\">code</a>). The combined corpus comprises 462,812 unique OpenAlex works (<a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8892b7-occupancy-is-not-integration-for-new/tree/fork/run_YczZzZ0_9kfq/round-2/dataset-5\">code</a>).</p>\n\n<h3>Co-word network</h3>\n<p>From a design-weighted background sample of 259,716 works, 25 yearly three-year-window co-occurrence snapshots were built (approximately 27,000 nodes and 84,000 edges per snapshot), with association-strength edge weights and Leiden community detection (<a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8892b7-occupancy-is-not-integration-for-new/tree/fork/run_YczZzZ0_9kfq/round-2/experiment-3\">code</a>). For each concept-keyword node, OpenAlex subfield-by-time-block publication counts supplied the host-vocabulary share used in RQ2, covering 78.7% of host co-occurrence weight across 1,372 nodes.</p>\n\n<h3>RQ1: Structural precursors of emergence</h3>\n<p>Sustained uptake is defined as reaching at least 20 papers per year with at least 20 percentile points of co-word network strength gain. Each concept showing sustained uptake is matched 1:1 to a control from the same first-appearance band and origin field. The standardised mean difference (Cohen's S) in closure measures during the pre-onset window is the estimand, with bootstrap confidence intervals (B = 2,000) and Holm-corrected p-values. Four closure variants were tested: general closure, turnover-residualised closure, persistent-neighbour closure (restricted to top-20 neighbours present in consecutive years), and Burt constraint.</p>\n\n<h3>RQ2: Host-entry grafting</h3>\n<p>A host-entry event is the first year a concept appears in a non-origin subfield together with at least five co-occurring partner terms. The host-vocabulary share measures the tag-weighted mean of each partner's pre-entry publication share in the host subfield. The outcome is five-year newcomer uptake: host-subfield papers by author-disjoint newcomers.</p>\n\n<p>Poisson pseudo-maximum-likelihood (PPML) regression with concept-clustered standard errors tests whether host-vocabulary share predicts uptake. Two specifications were pre-registered: a primary with concept&#xD7;year and host&#xD7;year fixed effects, and a co-primary with concept, entry-year and host fixed effects (used when the primary drops below 30 concept clusters). Co-transfer (fraction of partners that were origin companions) is included as a second regressor in both.</p>\n</section>\n\n<!-- RESULTS -->\n<section id=\"results\">\n<h2>Results</h2>\n\n<h3>Host-entry grafting</h3>\n\n<div class=\"res\">\n<div class=\"res-label\">MeSH replication (independent)</div>\n<div class=\"res-num\">IRR 1.23</div>\n<div class=\"res-ctx\">95% CI 1.12 to 1.36, p &lt; 0.001. Co-primary specification on 191 independent MeSH biomedical concepts (2,171 events, 160 concept clusters). Pre-registered verdict: REPLICATED. The primary specification is also significant (IRR 1.32, 95% CI 1.10 to 1.60, p = 0.004).</div>\n</div>\n\n<div class=\"res\">\n<div class=\"res-label\">Screen fold (development set)</div>\n<div class=\"res-num\">IRR 1.30</div>\n<div class=\"res-ctx\">95% CI 1.16 to 1.45, p &lt; 0.001. Co-primary specification, 1,544 events across 140 concept clusters.</div>\n</div>\n\n<div class=\"res\">\n<div class=\"res-label\">Held-out fold (development set)</div>\n<div class=\"res-num\">IRR 1.19</div>\n<div class=\"res-ctx\">95% CI 1.06 to 1.33, p = 0.004. Co-primary specification, 972 events across 74 concept clusters. Wild-cluster bootstrap p = 0.012, nativeness-permutation p = 0.026. The fully saturated primary specification is inconclusive (IRR 0.98, 95% CI 0.70 to 1.37, 30 clusters, p = 0.91), declared underpowered in advance.</div>\n</div>\n\n<div class=\"res\">\n<div class=\"res-label\">Pooled estimate (IVW, all three folds)</div>\n<div class=\"res-num\">IRR 1.26</div>\n<div class=\"res-ctx\">95% CI 1.17 to 1.36, I&sup2; = 0. One standard deviation of host-vocabulary share raises newcomer uptake by 26%.</div>\n</div>\n\n<div class=\"res\">\n<div class=\"res-label\">Co-transfer</div>\n<div class=\"res-num\">Null</div>\n<div class=\"res-ctx\">Null across all folds and specifications (p = 0.48, 0.60, and 0.053). Arriving with origin companions does not predict uptake.</div>\n</div>\n\n<h3>Margin decomposition</h3>\n<p>The host-vocabulary effect operates through both margins (<a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8892b7-occupancy-is-not-integration-for-new/tree/fork/run_YczZzZ0_9kfq/round-5/evaluation-6\">code</a>). The extensive margin (whether any uptake starts) accounts for 38% of the total effect (95% CI 21% to 55%): the pooled effect is +6.4 percentage points per SD (95% CI 4.8 to 8.1), approximately a 13% increase relative to the 51% base rate. The intensive margin (count of newcomer papers given uptake started) accounts for the remaining 62%, with a pooled IRR of 1.18 (95% CI 1.10 to 1.27).</p>\n\n<p>The host-vocabulary gradient is host-specific. Adding generality controls retains 97% of the coefficient (IVW retention 0.97, 95% CI 0.81 to 1.10). The Balassa-index lift measure is also significant (IVW IRR 1.34, 95% CI 1.23 to 1.46), though its within-fixed-effect correlation with the log of the continuous share is 0.997, so the lift test confirms the continuous measure rather than adding independent evidence (<a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8892b7-occupancy-is-not-integration-for-new/tree/fork/run_YczZzZ0_9kfq/round-5/evaluation-7\">code</a>). The Wald test for origin-field dependence is null (p = 0.64).</p>\n\n<h3>Structural precursors of emergence</h3>\n<p>On the Held-out fold (a development-set estimate), only persistent-neighbour closure survives Holm correction: S = &#x2212;1.07, 95% CI &#x2212;1.86 to &#x2212;0.29, Holm p = 0.015. General closure is not significant (Holm p = 0.147). Turnover-residualised closure is not significant (Holm p = 0.635). Burt constraint is positive (S = +0.11, 95% CI 0.02 to 0.19), indicating that emerging concepts sit in more constrained, not more brokered, ego networks (<a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8892b7-occupancy-is-not-integration-for-new/tree/fork/run_YczZzZ0_9kfq/round-3/experiment-5\">code</a>, <a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8892b7-occupancy-is-not-integration-for-new/tree/fork/run_YczZzZ0_9kfq/round-4/evaluation-3\">held-out check</a>).</p>\n\n<p>The MeSH replication of closure is directional under a sensitivity label (D = &#x2212;0.42, Holm p = 0.039, n = 29) but null under the primary label (D = &#x2212;0.09, Holm p = 0.677, n = 15) (<a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8892b7-occupancy-is-not-integration-for-new/tree/fork/run_YczZzZ0_9kfq/round-2/experiment-4\">code</a>). Structural precursors add no predictive value for sustained uptake beyond frequency, burst, degree and entropy baselines (logistic AUC 0.89 versus 0.88).</p>\n\n<h3>Adopter-level mechanism</h3>\n<p>Adopters are more likely to have prior corpus exposure to the concept's entry partners than matched non-adopters (conditional logistic regression: OR 3.09, prevalence 0.79 versus 0.61; 95% CI 2.32 to 4.28; 1,013 matched strata, 422 entries, 109 concepts; Screen fold, not independently confirmed) (<a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8892b7-occupancy-is-not-integration-for-new/tree/fork/run_YczZzZ0_9kfq/round-4/evaluation-5\">code</a>). Enrichment follows a vocabulary gradient: FOREIGN partners OR 2.88, ADJACENT OR 1.91, NATIVE OR 1.47.</p>\n\n<h3>Diffusion typology</h3>\n<p>A data-derived two-type typology (localised, n = 136, vs. broad from the start, n = 66; k-medoids, bootstrap minimum Jaccard 0.86) is stable, though it does not separate outcomes better than an entropy-only baseline. Among concepts with both observable onsets, expansion precedes diffusion in 25 of 26 pooled main-arm cases (proportion 0.96, 95% CI 0.81 to 1.00, p = 0.004) (<a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8892b7-occupancy-is-not-integration-for-new/tree/fork/run_YczZzZ0_9kfq/round-3/experiment-8\">code</a>, <a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8892b7-occupancy-is-not-integration-for-new/tree/fork/run_YczZzZ0_9kfq/round-4/evaluation-4\">unseen data check</a>).</p>\n\n<h3>Null findings</h3>\n<p>Co-transfer is null in all specifications and populations. The breadth-prediction screen (does openness predict how many subfields a concept reaches?) found no effect beyond growth and level baselines (<a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8892b7-occupancy-is-not-integration-for-new/tree/fork/run_YczZzZ0_9kfq/round-3/experiment-6\">code</a>). The link between pre-emergence closure and later host-entry composition is null (partial correlation 0.025 Screen, 0.053 Held-out, both CIs including zero).</p>\n</section>\n\n<!-- FIGURES -->\n<section id=\"figures\">\n<h2>Figures</h2>\n<div class=\"gallery\">\n\n<div class=\"gal-item\" tabindex=\"0\" role=\"button\" aria-label=\"Enlarge Figure 1: Study design and analysis pipeline\" data-lb-src=\"figures/fig1_v0.jpg\" data-lb-title=\"Figure 1. Study design and analysis pipeline\">\n<img src=\"figures/fig1_v0.jpg\" alt=\"Study design diagram with four panels: data sources, co-word network, matched event study for RQ1, and host-entry grafting framework for RQ2\" loading=\"lazy\">\n<div class=\"gal-cap\"><span class=\"gal-title\">Figure 1. Study design and analysis pipeline</span>\nOverview of the study design. (a) Data: an outcome-blind arXiv concept pool of 426 emerging scientific concepts, split into a screen fold (247) and a held-out fold (119), and an independent MeSH biomedical check population of 191 concepts. Both are drawn from 462,812 OpenAlex works. (b) Co-word network: yearly co-word snapshots (25 snapshots, ~27k nodes, ~84k edges) with Leiden communities. (c) RQ1, emergence precursors: a matched event study compares closure measures in the pre-onset window between concepts showing sustained uptake (blue, rising) and controls (grey, flat). Estimates on both main-arm folds are development-set estimates, not true held-out confirmations. The independent evidence comes from the MeSH replication.</p>\n</div>\n\n<div class=\"lim\">\n<strong>Population bias</strong>\n<p>The concept pool is dominated by physics, physical-sciences and computer-science concepts from arXiv. The MeSH population covers only biomedicine-to-biomedicine entries. Generalisation to social sciences, humanities or engineering is untested.</p>\n</div>\n\n<div class=\"lim\">\n<strong>Primary specification underpowered</strong>\n<p>The fully saturated specification with concept&#xD7;year and host&#xD7;year fixed effects is inconclusive on the Held-out fold (IRR 0.98, 30 clusters). The MeSH replication and development-set estimates rest on the co-primary specification, which absorbs less confounding.</p>\n</div>\n\n<div class=\"lim\">\n<strong>Single-paper entries</strong>\n<p>87% of co-primary Screen events involve a single entry-year paper. The pooled multi-team effect is positive (IRR 1.28, 95% CI 1.11 to 1.48), but the Held-out fold alone is underpowered for this test.</p>\n</div>\n\n<div class=\"lim\">\n<strong>Binary establishment null</strong>\n<p>Host-vocabulary share predicts the count of newcomer papers and the probability of any uptake, but binary establishment (at least five newcomer papers in at least three of five years) is null on the Held-out fold (p = 0.16). The effect is graded, not threshold-based.</p>\n</div>\n\n<div class=\"lim\">\n<strong>Cluster-robust inference</strong>\n<p>The cluster-robust variance estimator rejects 10% to 11% of null shuffles in simulation (target 5%). Wild-cluster bootstrap and permutation tests give consistent results (Held-out wild p = 0.012, permutation p = 0.026), but standard p-values should not be taken at face value.</p>\n</div>\n\n<div class=\"lim\">\n<strong>Host-specificity caveat</strong>\n<p>The Balassa-index lift measure has a within-fixed-effect correlation of 0.997 with the log of the continuous host-vocabulary share. The lift test confirms the continuous measure rather than providing independent evidence for host-specificity.</p>\n</div>\n\n<div class=\"lim\">\n<strong>Adopter evidence not confirmed</strong>\n<p>The adopter-level enrichment (OR 3.09) is Screen-fold only, not independently confirmed. The design cannot separate absorptive capacity from topical proximity.</p>\n</div>\n\n<div class=\"lim\">\n<strong>Closure caveats</strong>\n<p>The Held-out fold was used in pipeline development, so the closure result is a development-set estimate. The Held-out matching falls back to Screen controls for 17 of 25 unique controls. The MeSH closure result is directional under the sensitivity label but null under the primary label.</p>\n</div>\n</section>\n\n<!-- CODE LIST (artifacts not discussed elsewhere) -->\n<section from playwright.async_api import async_playwright
import sys, os

async def main():

        await page_m.goto(f"file://{PAGE}", wait_until="networkidle")
        await page_m.wait_for_timeout(500)
        await page_m.screenshot(path=os.path.join(OUT_DIR, "mobile_full.png"), full_page=True)
        await ctx_m.close()

        # Desktop width (1280px) - top
        ctx_d = await browser.new_context(viewport={"width": 1280, "height": 900}, device_scale_factor=2)
        page_d = await ctx_d.new_page()
        await page_d.goto(f"file://{PAGE}", wait_until="networkidle")
        await page_d.wait_for_timeout(500)
        await page_d.screenshot(path=os.path.join(OUT_DIR, "desktop_top.png"))

        # Desktop - scroll to middle
        total_h = await page_d.evaluate("document.body.scrollHeight")
        await page_d.evaluate(f"window.scrollTo(0, {total_h // 2})")
        await page_d.wait_for_timeout(300)
        await page_d.screenshot(path=os.path.join(OUT_DIR, "desktop_mid.png"))

        # Desktop - scroll to end
        await page_d.evaluate(f"window.scrollTo(0, {total_h})")
        await page_d.wait_for_timeout(300)
        await page_d.screenshot(path=os.path.join(OUT_DIR, "desktop_end.png"))

        await ctx_d.close()
        await browser.close()

asyncio.run(main())

import asyncio
from playwright.async_api import async_playwright
import os

PAGE = "/ai-inventor/aii_data/runs/run_YczZzZ0_9kfq/4_gen_paper_repo/_4_assemble_paper/paper/index.html"
OUT = "/tmp/claude-10001/-ai-inventor-aii-data-runs-run-YczZzZ0-9kfq-4-gen-paper-repo--4-assemble-paper-paper/5a4aa0b2-0870-472c-bbcf-8ba8ab12076b/scratchpad/shots"

async def main():

        browser = await p.chromium.launch(
            executable_path="/usr/bin/chromium-headless-shell",
            args=["--no-sandbox", "--disable-gpu"]
        )
        ctx = await browser.new_context(viewport={"width": 1280, "height": 900})
        page = await ctx.new_page()
        await page.goto(f"file://{PAGE}", wait_until="networkidle")
        await page.wait_for_timeout(500)

        # Test 1: Tab to skip link
        await page.keyboard.press("Tab")
        focused = await page.evaluate("document.activeElement.className")
        print(f"First Tab -> class='{focused}' (expect 'skip')")

        # Test 2: Tab through nav links
        for i in range(6):
            await page.keyboard.press("Tab")
        focused_tag = await page.evaluate("document.activeElement.tagName")
        focused_href = await page.evaluate("document.activeElement.getAttribute('href')")
        print(f"After 7 tabs -> {focused_tag} href={focused_href}")

        # Test 3: Tab to first gallery item and open lightbox
        await page.evaluate("document.querySelector('.gal-item').focus()")
        await page.keyboard.press("Enter")
        await page.wait_for_timeout(300)
        lb_open = await page.evaluate("document.getElementById('lightbox').classList.contains('open')")
        print(f"Lightbox open after Enter on gallery item: {lb_open}")

        # Test 4: Screenshot lightbox
        if lb_open:
            await page.screenshot(path=os.path.join(OUT, "lightbox_open.png"))

            # Focus should be on close button
            focused_class = await page.evaluate("document.activeElement.className")
            print(f"Focus in lightbox: class='{focused_class}' (expect 'lb-close')")

            # Tab should stay on close button (focus trap)
            await page.keyboard.press("Tab")
            focused_class2 = await page.evaluate("document.activeElement.className")
            print(f"After Tab in lightbox: class='{focused_class2}' (expect 'lb-close')")

            # Escape should close
            await page.keyboard.press("Escape")
            await page.wait_for_timeout(300)
            lb_open2 = await page.evaluate("document.getElementById('lightbox').classList.contains('open')")
            print(f"Lightbox closed after Escape: {not lb_open2}")

        # Test 5: Check focus returned to trigger
        focused_role = await page.evaluate("document.activeElement.getAttribute('role')")
        print(f"Focus returned to trigger: role='{focused_role}' (expect 'button')")

        # Test 6: Verify focus ring styles exist
        has_focus_visible = await page.evaluate("""
            (() => {
                for (let sheet of document.styleSheets) {
                    for (let rule of sheet.cssRules) {
                        if (rule.selectorText && rule.selectorText.includes('focus-visible')) return true;
                    }
                }
                return false;
            })()
        """)
        print(f"Has :focus-visible styles: {has_focus_visible}")

        await ctx.close()
        await browser.close()

asyncio.run(main())
```

# Paper: Host vocabulary predicts whether new scientific concepts take root across disciplinary boundaries

This directory contains the final paper and its public web page.

## Layout

- `paper.tex` — LaTeX source of the final paper.
- `paper.pdf` — Compiled paper PDF.
- `references.bib` — Bibliography.
- `references.json` — Bibliography in JSON format.
- `figures/` — All paper figures: two JPGs (fig1, fig2) and four PNGs rendered from PDF originals (fig3–fig6).
- `index.html` — Self-contained public web page (GitHub Pages site) summarising the paper.
- `workspace/` — LaTeX compilation scratch directory (can be removed).

## Running

The web page is a single self-contained HTML file with no dependencies. Open `index.html` in any browser. All figures are referenced as `figures/filename` and must be in the same relative position.

To recompile the paper:

```bash
cd workspace
pdflatex paper.tex
bibtex paper
pdflatex paper.tex
pdflatex paper.tex
```

## Restoring removed files

The `workspace/` directory is regenerated by running the LaTeX compilation commands above.

        await browser.close()

asyncio.run(main())
